barriers.reason: The patient is the only person who walks Danny to the bus at 8:30 AM, which directly conflicts with a 9:00 AM cardiac rehab start three mornings a week, and the sister in Skokie can help only occasionally, not three days a week.

alternatives.text: Ask cardiac rehab for a later start time or different days so sessions do not conflict with the 8:30 AM school bus drop-off.
Schedule rehab sessions on the same day and campus as other appointments to reduce separate trips and caregiving strain.

barriers.reason: Power has been off since Monday with lights and the fridge off, so the patient cannot charge a Bluetooth scale or cuff or upload daily readings through the heart failure app.

alternatives.text: Obtain weights and blood pressure at clinic visits instead of relying on daily home app uploads while power is out.
Have the patient continue the written daily weight log they already keep (turn:T14) and review it at visits until power is restored.

barriers.reason: CPAP requires electricity nightly and ComEd cut power since Monday, leaving the patient sleeping sitting up in a chair without the machine.

alternatives.text: Complete the utility medical certification form because the patient's health depends on power for CPAP, to delay disconnection.
Apply for LIHEAP utility assistance through CEDA in Cook County to help restore power.
